vBRIEFInfo.author: agent:deft-directive-setup
vBRIEFInfo.description: E2E: WebRTC via node-datachannel — real DTLS/SCTP loopback between two in-process PeerConnections

narratives.Description: Add a real WebRTC DataChannel E2E test using the node-datachannel npm package (npm install --save-dev node-datachannel), which provides Node.js bindings for libdatachannel. Two PeerConnection instances are created in the same process and ICE negotiation is wired in-process via loopback (no STUN/TURN server required for loopback). Setup: (1) Create pc1 and pc2 with iceServers: []. (2) Wire ICE: pc1.onLocalDescription → pc2.setRemoteDescription, pc2.onLocalDescription → pc1.setRemoteDescription, pc1.onLocalCandidate → pc2.addRemoteCandidate, pc2.onLocalCandidate → pc1.addRemoteCandidate. (3) pc1.createDataChannel('omux/control', { protocol: 'x-xumux' }) — this triggers ICE negotiation. (4) Wait for pc2.onDataChannel to fire with the server-side DataChannel. (5) Wrap each DataChannel with WebRTCAdapter (dc must implement DataChannelLike — may require a thin shim for the node-datachannel API surface). (6) Create XumuxClient + XumuxServer on the two adapters and run the 5 standard E2E protocol scenarios. Shim requirements: node-datachannel uses onmessage, onclose, onopen callbacks (not addEventListener) — the WebRTCAdapter may need a thin adapter shim or node-datachannel may support addEventListener. Check node-datachannel API docs and implement accordingly. Add task e2e:webrtc:native to Taskfile.yml. Note: node-datachannel is a native binary (~15 MB per platform); CI matrix must include platform-specific builds.
narratives.Traces: FR-14 (WebRTC DataChannel adapter), NFR-5 (optional peer dependencies for transport adapters)
narratives.Files: tests/e2e/webrtc-native.e2e.test.ts (new), tests/e2e/node-dc-shim.ts (thin DataChannelLike shim for node-datachannel API), Taskfile.yml (add e2e:webrtc:native task), package.json (add node-datachannel devDep)
narratives.Acceptance: task e2e:webrtc:native exits 0 on macOS, Linux, and Windows. All 5 protocol scenarios pass over a real DTLS/SCTP connection. ICE negotiation completes within 10 seconds.
